# Ground-truth byte layouts for the ESP-NOW wire structs.
#
# Generated by tools/golden/gen_golden.cpp, which carries the enow_text_msg_t
# and enow_admin_msg_t typedefs verbatim from the firmware's src/WiFiOps.h and
# lets a real C++ compiler lay them out.
#
# Two exceptions, marked where they appear: the `admin*` vectors are wartui's
# own fourteen-byte MSG_ADMIN, which no C++ typedef describes because no vendor
# firmware speaks it, and the captured frames at the bottom came off the air.
# Regenerating replaces only the block above the first blank line.
#
# Format: <name> <length> <hex>.  Lines starting with # are ignored, so output
# from tools/espnow-sniffer can be pasted in unedited to turn frames captured
# off the air into permanent regression tests.
heartbeat 212 
text_wifi 212 
text_ble 212 
core_request 212 
legacy_admin 10 454e4f57050702051017

# --- wartui's own MSG_ADMIN --------------------------------------------------
# Hand-written, not generated: from Phase 2 the core -> node frame is ours. It
# is fourteen bytes and carries a forty-bit channel mask where the vendor's ten
# carried a pair of bounds.
#
# `admin` is `legacy_admin`'s fields said the new way -- same version, index and
# count, and the mask holding exactly the indices 16..=23 that frame's bounds
# named. Reading the two side by side is the whole of what changed.
#
# `admin_ble` pins the parts a range could not have: the BLE flag set, and a
# mask whose bits are deliberately spread -- 0, 6, 13 and 39 -- so a byte-order
# mistake in the five little-endian bytes cannot pass.
admin 14 454e4f5705070205000000ff0000
admin_ble 14 454e4f5705c80001014120000080

# --- Frames captured off real hardware, 2026-09-05 ---------------------------
# ESP32-C5 node (firmware v2.3.2) paired with a C5 wardriver core, sniffed by a
# C6 on channel 6. Plaintext, broadcast to FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF, RSSI about -40.
# Heartbeat counters 147-151 are a node roughly twelve minutes into its run,
# which is why every observation here is BLE: nearby access points had long
# since been absorbed into the node's 200-entry dedup ring.
